proof.text: Replace the specified cartesian square by the canonical pullback via H.isoPullback. The second projection is smooth because it is the composite of the inverse comparison isomorphism with c. Quasi-compactness of p over the Noetherian stage makes P compact. Take P.affineCover.finiteSubcover; each chart is affine and its composite to the base remains locally finitely presented, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated.

The limit base change of each source chart is smooth: by pullbackRightPullbackFstIso it is the composite of the pulled-back open immersion with the smooth canonical projection. Apply affine-source eventual smoothness to each of these finitely many charts, obtaining stages js k in Over i.

Use IsCofiltered.inf_objs_exists on the finite image of js in Over i to obtain j with a map to every js k. The equation Over.w identifies X.map j.hom with the composite transition through js k. The iso pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso identifies each chart at j with the further base change of its smooth chart at js k, hence it is smooth. Finally pull back the finite source cover along the canonical first projection. pullbackRightPullbackFstIso identifies its restricted second projections with those smooth charts. IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover proves smoothness of the whole second projection. This works also for an empty finite cover, since Over i is nonempty.

title: Eventual smoothness over an arbitrary affine-transition limit
statement: Let $I$ be a small cofiltered category and $X:I\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ a diagram with affine transition morphisms and Noetherian quasi-separated stages [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\alpha:S\to X$ be a limiting cone. Fix $i\in I$ and a morphism $p:P\to X_i$ that is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $c:C\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $a:C\to P$ give a cartesian square $(a,c,p,\alpha_i)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist an object $j\in I$ and an arrow $f:j\to i$ such that $P\times_{X_i}X_j\to X_j$ is smooth.

theorem exists_smooth_stage_of_affine_limit {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I]
    [IsCofiltered I] {S C : Scheme.{u}}
    (X : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (α : (Functor.const I).obj S ⟶ X)
    (hα : IsLimit (Cone.mk S α))
    (hXa : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (X.map f))
    (hN : ∀ i, IsNoetherian (X.obj i))
    (hqs : ∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (X.obj i))
    {i : I} {P : Scheme.{u}} (p : P ⟶ X.obj i)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    (c : C ⟶ S) [Smooth c] (a : C ⟶ P)
    (H : IsPullback a c p (α.app i)) :
    ∃ j : Over i, Smooth (pullback.snd p (X.map j.hom))
